2. The facts bearing upon this Rule are that the petitioner No.1 A.B.M. Shamsul Alam who was Manager of the Agrani Bank, Santi Nagar Branch, Dhaka from 19.1237 to 23.11.79, was indicated in Special Case No. 74 of 19 arising out of Motijheel P.S. Case No. 147(4) 80 in the Court of Special Judge Dhaka, under section 409 Cr.P.C read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 with allegation that during the said period, the petitioner in the capacity of the manager of the branch, in flagrant violation of the Rules and Regulation and direction of the Head Office, allowed unauthorized temporary clear over drafts in the different accounts of the Bank both current and savings, to the tune of Tk. 15,13,643.20 paisa. He suppressed the aforesaid unauthorized over-drafts in his monthly statements. It was also alleged that the petitioner No.1 allowed drawing of cash credit accounts of the different, parties without taking any goods into pledge and also issued bank guarantee to different parties without any authority and sanction from the Head Office. Upon the investigation, the police submitted charge sheet against the petitioner No. I and the petitioner No. 2 and another A.H.M. Ahmed Hossain who is dead, under section 109 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of Act 11/47. After passing through different courts, the records of the case were received by the Special Judge, Dhaka Division, Dhaka, on 15.3.84 for disposal and he took cognizance of the case under section 409 of the Penal Code. Eventually on 6.1.87 when the case was taken up for examination of witnesses, the petitioner No. 2 and another co moved an application under section 339-C of the Code of Criminal Procedure for stopping the proceeding and releasing the accused. The learned Special Judge rejected the prayer on 4.2.87 in view of the provisions of Ordinance No. 3 of 1987 which were applicable to the instant case On 7.10.79 the petitioner No. 2 and another co-accused made an application under section 8(A) of Ordinance No. 3 of 1987 for stopping the proceeding of the case and releasing the accused. On 15.12.89 the Government directed the Special Public Prosecutor for taking steps for restoration of the case which stood stopped by an order on 15.1099. Accordingly on. 1.1.1990 the Special Public Prosecutor, Dhaka, filed an application for restoration of the case and the learned Special Judge restored the case by his order on the same date. 

 4. Mr. Fazlul Karim the learned Advocate for the petitioners has submitted that the prosecution of the petitioners having been stopped on 15.10.89 under section 8(A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, restoration of the same on 1.1.1990 under the provision of section 339-D is without jurisdiction. He has submitted that the provisions of section 339-D of the Code of Criminal Procedure are inconsistent with the provision of section 8(A) of the Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance, 1987 (Ordinance III of 1987) which came into force on the 20th January, 1987, and was made to Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1987 with effect from the date providing for a special and definite period of limitation for conclusion of trial of those cases under Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 which were pending on the date of commencement of the Ordinance. He has submitted that the proceeding of the instant case had been finally and the accused had been released on 15.9.89 after expiry of 2 years from the date of commencement of the Ordinance III of 1987 which period was specially provided by amendment of the Special Law, Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. 

 5. Elaborating his argument, he has submitted that consideration of sections 1 and 2 of the Criminal Procedure Code along with section 5(2) of the Code makes it clear that the provision of Criminal Procedure Code will not apply where there has been special procedure provided in the Special Law. It is only section 6(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, which makes the Code of Criminal Procedure applicable to the cases under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, only when the same is not inconsistent with the provisions of the said Act. 

 7. Now, Section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 is as follows:- 

 Therefore it is for us to consider whether section 339-D of the Code of Criminal Procedure making provisions of revival of the criminal cases introduced by Ordinance No. 23 of 1986 dated 27.3.86 are inconsistent with the provision of Section 8(A) of the Criminal Law Amendment (Amendment) Ordinance No. III of 1987 which was embodied in the Act XIII 1987. Section 339D sub-section (1) of the Criminal Procedure Code provides for revival of criminal cases of which proceeding have been stopped and accused released in terms of section 339-C of the Code. In the instant case we have seen from the above narration of the proceeding that the case had been revived, upon a prayer by the public prosecutor at the, instance of the Government by the court concerned clearly within 90 days from the date of its stoppage. Now there could not be any illegality about this order if it can be found that section 8(A) of the of Ordinance III of 1987 corresponding to Act 13 of 1987 which came into force On 20.1.87 was in conflict with the provision of section 339-D of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It is true that Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, is a special law and if there is any provision in this law inconsistent with provision of the section 339—D or express or implied for revival of the case stopped under section 8(A) of Ordinance III of 1987 of Act 13 of 1987 which is an amending of Criminal Law Amendment Act; 1958. 

 8. The very section quoted above shows that it was meant for continuation of trial of certain Special Cases within a specified period notwithstanding their stopping in accordance with section 339C of the Code. The cases which have been stopped or ought to have been stopped under section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure before commencement of Ordinance III of 1987 or Act XIII of 1987 which came into force on 20.1.87 After disposal of each, section 8 outlines its purpose. On a clear reading of this section it appears to us that the application under section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure was not taken out by this amending section. It rather enlarged the period for stopping of the proceeding. To our mind this section 8(A) was not substitution of section 339C governing the cases under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. Rather it was supplemental to section 339C enlarging the period of limitation for disposal of Special Cases under the Criminal Law Amendment Act to which the principle of section 339C of the Criminal Procedure Code applied by dint of Section 6(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act. After passage of years from the date of commencement of the Act, XIII/37 (or the Ordinance No. IIII/87) the application of 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure, remain applicable to the cases under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 in view of section 6(1) of the later act sub-section (b) of section 8 also shows that the legislature considers what cases should be considered as concluded and should never to be revived. There is no mention in section 8 that once in accordance with section 8(A) stopped such cases should never be revived re opened. In other words we do not find any express provision in section 8 of the Ordinance 3/87 or Act 13/87 barring revival of cases which have been stopped under section 8(a). 

 9. Mr. Fazlul Karim, learned Advocate for the petitioner has argued that having regard to the mischief of section 339C requiring stoppage proceedings only when the legislature introduced section 8(a) of the Ordinance 3/87 and Act 13/87 in order to give sufficient time for disposal of the cases under the Criminal Law Amendment Act of 1958, the legislature ought to give sufficient time, finally, for disposal of the cases pending at the time of Ordinance on 20.1.87 and therefore, no further time should be available for the prosecution and disposal of such cases. Mr. Fazlul Karim also, argued that the proceedings of The instant case was not stopped under section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure but section 8(a) of Act XIII of 1987 which is a special law, but 339D referred only to proceedings of such cases as are stopped under Section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure but section 8(a) of Act XIII of 1987 which is a special law; but 3391) referred only to proceedings of such cases as are stopped under section 339C; of the Code of Criminal Procedure Therefore 339D has no application for revival of the cases of Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958. Mr. Shamsul Karim, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the State in reply submits that the instant case was stopped in accordance with Section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure as modified or supplemented by section 8 of Act Xlii of 1987. Therefore the expression "cases stopped" under sub-section 4 of section 339C will not preclude operation of 339D in respect of cases under Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. 

 10. We have considered the arguments on this point very carefully and we are of the view that the sec. 339D of Criminal Procedure Code will not be precluded from operation in cases under Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 merely because 339C mentions the cases stopped under sub-section 8(a) of the Act XIII/87 has really modified the section 339C which is applicable in respect of cases under the Criminal Law Amendment Act in view of section 6(1) of the said Act. 

 11. Mr Shamsul Karim, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the State has further argued that in view of section 6(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, the provisions of Criminal Procedure Code is applicable to any case under the Act for any purpose if they are not inconsistent with the provisions of Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 Therefore logically this provision of Section 339D of the Code of Criminal Procedure will be the only provision available for revival of cases under the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 and no question of inconsistency arises. He has argued that it is to be noticed that section 8(A) of the Ordinance III and Act XIII/87 speaks of stoppage of the proceeding and release of the accused and not of acquittal or discharge when the case is stopped and the accused are released, it must be said that the proceeding is not concluded either way, it remains in a moribund condition. The expressions "stopped" and "released" indicate that the legislature did not intend to exclude revival of appropriate cases under Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, after they were Stopped in accordance with Section 8 of Ordinance Ill of 1987. Indeed such contention would be again the spirit of criminal jurisprudence. Our Appellate Division in the case to Niamat Ali Sheikh and others Vs.
